sheets.name: Control Matrix
rows: 14 controls across input, output, human, posting and monitoring layers
REV-AI-2026-01 | Meridian Harbor Software, Inc. (fictional) | FY2026 Q4 close readiness | Fictional data
Use-case approval and annual AI risk assessment
Keep the deployed use case inside an approved scope and risk appetite.

CFO and Controller approve the use case, model, data classes and authority limits each January. Any expansion of scope needs a new approval. Risk assessment refreshed annually and after material change.
Model, prompt and schema change control
Prevent untested changes from altering extraction or conclusions.
Changes to model, prompt or output schema require a change ticket, regression test on the 50-contract golden set, and Controller approval. Version identifiers are recorded on every output.
Vendor due diligence and subprocessor review
Obtain assurance over the vendor's controls, data handling and continuity.

Annual review of SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II reports, bridge letter, data processing agreement, subprocessor list and model-training attestation. Complementary user entity controls are mapped to Meridian Harbor controls.
Ensure the model and reviewer see the complete executed agreement.
Intake checklist confirms executed signature, all exhibits and amendments present, native PDF where available, and no draft watermarks. Incomplete packages are returned to Legal before inference.
Keep personal and confidential data out of model prompts and logs.

Automated entity detection masks names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, bank details and government identifiers before inference. Redaction log retained. Vendor logging is configured to masked text only and attested in the annual review.
Restrict who can submit, review, change settings or post revenue.

Role-based access to the contract repository and model workspace; quarterly access review; no user can both submit a contract and approve its revenue schedule. Model settings require two administrators.
Structured output with citations and abstention
Force every extracted term to be traceable, and permit the model to abstain.

Output schema requires clause citation, character span, page number, confidence and an explicit flag for missing information or suspicious text. The model must not produce an allocation when required inputs are absent.
Verify allocation arithmetic and the effective SSP table outside the model.

A deterministic calculator recomputes relative SSP allocation and the revenue schedule from approved inputs. A second analyst re-performs the calculation and confirms the SSP table version effective on the contract date.
Have a qualified reviewer agree each material term to the cited clause before posting.

Reviewer opens each cited clause, confirms the extracted term, records an annotation per judgment field and signs off in the workflow with SSO identity and timestamp. Output cannot move to posting without sign-off.
Add a second qualified reviewer where the risk of a wrong conclusion is highest.

Mandatory second-level review when TCV is at least $250,000, any non-standard term flag is present, confidence is below 0.70, a new SKU or pricing model is used, or the contract modifies an existing arrangement.
Ensure only approved revenue schedules reach the general ledger.

Controller approves the final schedule in the revenue subledger. Journal entries post through the standard workflow with preparer, approver and schedule reference. The model has no write access to the ERP.
Monthly QA sample and accuracy metrics
Detect degradation and confirm that review controls work over time.

Each month, 10 closed contracts are re-performed independently and scored on 10 fields. Accuracy, agreement and exception trends are reported to the Controller; a drop below 92% field accuracy or any uncaught judgment error triggers escalation.
Exception log, root cause and remediation tracking
Make sure every error is logged, traced to a cause and fixed.

All extraction errors, override disagreements and reviewer findings are logged with contract, field, root cause and owner. Open items are reviewed monthly by the Controller and quarterly by the Audit Committee.
Keep the process running if the model changes or the vendor exits.
Monitor vendor end-of-life notices, model version retirements and subprocessor changes. Maintain a documented manual fallback, contract exit terms and a tested transition plan for model replacement.

sheets.name: Findings
rows: Condition, criteria, cause and effect for each finding
REV-AI-2026-01 | Meridian Harbor Software, Inc. (fictional) | FY2026 Q4 close readiness | Fictional data
Prompt template v3.2 was deployed on 2026-08-14 without documented regression testing or Controller approval.
Policy AI-CHG-02 requires regression testing on the 50-contract golden set and Controller sign-off for prompt changes.
Change-ticket template lost the test-evidence field during a workflow migration; the approver did not notice.

Retroactive testing under v3.1 and v3.2 produced one intended difference, on the prompt-injection test (C-2026-013); the other 24 outputs were unchanged, so no misstatement. The control did not operate as designed.
Restore the test-evidence field and add an automated gate; run retroactive regression tests for v3.1 and v3.2; Controller approval required for all prompt changes.
The calculator selected the SSP table marked current at run time rather than the table effective on the contract date.
ASC 606-10-32-28 through 38 and policy REV-SSP-04 require the SSP table effective on the contract date.
The FY2026 table was loaded on 2026-02-03, after two January contracts had been processed.
Allocation variances of $18,400 (C-2026-005) and $6,900 (C-2026-024) were found by manual re-performance and corrected before posting.
Add effective-date parameters and an automated table-version reconciliation; require 100% manual check for contracts executed before 2026-02-03 until the fix is live.
2 of 25 review sign-offs (8%) had no clause-level annotation for judgment fields, exceeding the 5% tolerable rate.
Policy REV-AI-07 requires a recorded annotation for each judgment field before sign-off.
The workflow allowed sign-off with an empty annotation field; reviewers skipped it when the model output looked routine. The same issue was flagged by QA in August 2026 and recurred in September.
Evidence is insufficient to show that review occurred for those two files. Re-performance found no financial error in either file.
Make annotation a mandatory field enforced by the workflow; retrain reviewers; apply 100% second-level review for 60 days; add the metric to the monthly QA report.
Vendor debug logging retained raw contract text, including personal data, for 30 days.
DPA Section 5.3 limits vendor processing to masked text and requires deletion within 24 hours.
A default debug setting was enabled during a vendor-side troubleshooting session on 2026-08-21.
No evidence of access or disclosure. Log retention was disabled on 2026-09-02 and the vendor issued a deletion certificate on 2026-09-19.
Amend the DPA to require configuration attestation in the bridge letter; add logging configuration to the annual vendor review and to CL-05.

sheets.name: Observations
rows: Matters noted in testing that do not rise to a control finding
REV-AI-2026-01 | Meridian Harbor Software, Inc. (fictional) | FY2026 Q4 close readiness | Fictional data

The model extracted the non-appropriation clause but did not flag it as non-standard. CL-09 caught the omission. Add the clause pattern to the model's non-standard clause library; no control change required.
Missing exhibits and scanned documents raise review effort and reliance on abstention. Require native PDFs in CL-04 and add an OCR pre-processing step to the intake checklist.

Review time fell 62% (4.2 to 1.6 hours per contract), which raises automation-bias risk. Make the monthly QA re-performance blind: the QA reviewer should form a conclusion before seeing the model output.

sheets.name: NIST Mapping
rows: Applicability and treatment for the 12 named GenAI risks
REV-AI-2026-01 | Meridian Harbor Software, Inc. (fictional) | FY2026 Q4 close readiness | Fictional data
Contract review cannot produce chemical, biological, radiological or nuclear capability.
Primary risk. Fabricated or misquoted terms and citations. Addressed by CL-07 citations, CL-09 reconciliation, CL-12 QA, and TC-01 to TC-09.
No content generation to third parties; contract review output is internal and structured.
Contract text contains signatory and guarantor personal data. Addressed by CL-05 redaction, CL-03 DPA terms and F-04 remediation.
Inference volume is about 240 contracts a year. Energy use is not separately metered and is immaterial to the process; it is not a control objective.
Accuracy may vary with document format, scan quality and language. Addressed by CL-04 intake, CL-07 confidence and CL-10 routing; TC-14 covers the scanned-document case.
Automation bias and over-trust in confidence scores. Addressed by CL-09 annotations, CL-10 triggers, CL-12 blind re-performance and O-03.
A wrong conclusion enters the financial statements if review fails. Addressed by the full control chain and the evidence pack.
Hidden text or prompt injection in contract files. Addressed by CL-07 flags, CL-09 review and TC-10.
Customer contract text could be used for training. Addressed by the DPA training prohibition and annual attestation under CL-03.
The workflow does not generate content for publication or for individuals.
Vendor model changes, deprecation and reference-data drift. Addressed by CL-02, CL-03, CL-08 and CL-14.
